source.text: וְלֹֽא־יָכֹ֨ל יוֹסֵ֜ף לְהִתְאַפֵּ֗ק לְכֹ֤ל הַנִּצָּבִים֙ עָלָ֔יו וַיִּקְרָ֕א הוֹצִ֥יאוּ כָל־אִ֖ישׁ מֵעָלָ֑י וְלֹא־עָ֤מַד אִישׁ֙ אִתּ֔וֹ בְּהִתְוַדַּ֥ע יוֹסֵ֖ף אֶל־אֶחָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And not was able Joseph to restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he called out, send out every man from with me. And not stood any man with him when made himself known Joseph to his brothers.

en.L: And Joseph could not restrain himself before all who stood by him, and he cried out, "Make everyone go out from me!" So no one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
en.B: Joseph could hold back no longer in front of all the attendants around him. "Send everyone out of here!" he cried. So he was alone with his brothers when he told them who he was.
en.R: Joseph could not keep his feelings in any longer in front of his servants. He shouted, "Everyone, leave the room!" So no one else was there when Joseph told his brothers who he was.

es.L: Y José no pudo contenerse delante de todos los que estaban junto a él, y gritó: «¡{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} salir a todos de mi lado!». Así que nadie estaba con él cuando José se dio a conocer a sus hermanos.
es.B: José ya no pudo contener la emoción delante de todos los que lo atendían. «¡{{plural_you:Saquen|Sacad}} a todos de aquí!», gritó. Así se quedó a solas con sus hermanos cuando les reveló quién era.
es.R: José ya no podía aguantar más lo que sentía delante de sus sirvientes. Gritó: «¡Que salgan todos de aquí!». Así que no había nadie más cuando José les dijo a sus hermanos quién era.

fr.L: Et Joseph ne put se contenir devant tous ceux qui se tenaient près de lui, et il s’écria : « Faites sortir tout le monde d’auprès de moi ! » Ainsi, personne ne resta avec lui quand Joseph se fit connaître à ses frères.
fr.B: Joseph ne put se maîtriser plus longtemps devant tous ceux qui le servaient. « Faites sortir tout le monde d’ici ! » s’écria-t-il. Il se trouva donc seul avec ses frères quand il leur révéla qui il était.
fr.R: Joseph n’arrivait plus à cacher ce qu’il ressentait devant ses serviteurs. Il a crié : « Sortez tous de la pièce ! » Alors il n’y avait plus personne d’autre quand Joseph a dit à ses frères qui il était.

sw.L: Naye Yusufu hakuweza kujizuia mbele ya wote waliosimama karibu naye, akapiga kelele, "Toeni kila mtu mbele yangu!" Kwa hiyo hakuna mtu aliyesimama pamoja naye Yusufu alipojitambulisha kwa ndugu zake.
sw.B: Yusufu hakuweza tena kujizuia mbele ya watumishi wote waliomzunguka. Akapaza sauti, "Watoeni watu wote humu!" Basi akabaki peke yake na ndugu zake alipowaambia yeye ni nani.
sw.R: Yusufu hakuweza kuficha hisia zake tena mbele ya watumishi wake. Akapiga kelele, "Kila mtu atoke chumbani!" Kwa hiyo hapakuwa na mtu mwingine pale Yusufu alipowaambia ndugu zake yeye ni nani.

decisions.choice: restrain himself: hold in his feelings
decisions.reason: The same verb described Joseph controlling himself after weeping in 43:31. Now he can no longer hold back.

decisions.choice: made himself known: revealed his identity
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of yada, "know": Joseph lets himself be known. He does it in private, with no Egyptian witnesses to his brothers' shame.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("ne put", "s'écria", "se fit connaître"); passé composé at Readable ("a crié", "a dit")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of school reading today. Speech keeps the passé composé at every level.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֶת־קֹל֖וֹ בִּבְכִ֑י וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע בֵּ֥ית פַּרְעֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave his voice in weeping, and heard Egypt, and heard [the] house of Pharaoh.

en.L: And he wept aloud, and the Egyptians heard, and the household of Pharaoh heard.
en.B: He wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard it, and word of it reached Pharaoh's household.
en.R: He cried so loudly that the Egyptians outside heard him. Even the people in Pharaoh's palace heard about it.

es.L: Y lloró a gritos, y [lo] oyeron los egipcios, y [lo] oyó la casa del faraón.
es.B: Lloró tan fuerte que los egipcios lo oyeron, y la noticia llegó hasta la casa del faraón.
es.R: Lloró tan alto que lo oyeron los egipcios que estaban afuera. Hasta la gente del palacio del faraón se enteró.

fr.L: Et il pleura à grands cris, et les Égyptiens [l’]entendirent, et la maison de Pharaon [l’]entendit.
fr.B: Il pleura si fort que les Égyptiens l’entendirent, et la nouvelle parvint jusqu’à la maison de Pharaon.
fr.R: Il a pleuré si fort que les Égyptiens qui étaient dehors l’ont entendu. Même les gens du palais de Pharaon en ont entendu parler.

sw.L: Akalia kwa sauti kubwa, na Wamisri wakasikia, na nyumba ya Farao ikasikia.
sw.B: Alilia kwa sauti kubwa mno hata Wamisri wakasikia, na habari zikafika nyumbani kwa Farao.
sw.R: Alilia kwa sauti kubwa sana hata Wamisri waliokuwa nje wakamsikia. Hata watu wa ikulu ya Farao walisikia habari hiyo.

decisions.choice: gave his voice in weeping: wept aloud
decisions.reason: To "give one's voice" is to raise it; Joseph sobs out loud. This is the third and fullest time he weeps over his brothers (42:24; 43:30).

decisions.choice: Egypt heard: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The name of the country stands for its people, here those in and around Joseph's house.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ אֲנִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף הַע֥וֹד אָבִ֖י חָ֑י וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֤וּ אֶחָיו֙ לַעֲנ֣וֹת אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִבְהֲל֖וּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joseph to his brothers, I [am] Joseph; [is] still my father living? And not were able his brothers to answer him, for they were terrified before him.

en.L: And Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?" But his brothers could not answer him, for they were terrified at his presence.
en.B: "I am Joseph!" he said to his brothers. "Is my father really still alive?" His brothers were too shaken to say a word, dismayed to be standing before him.
en.R: Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?" But his brothers could not say anything. They were too frightened of him.

es.L: Y dijo José a sus hermanos: «Yo [soy] José. ¿Vive todavía mi padre?». Pero sus hermanos no pudieron responderle, porque estaban aterrados ante él.
es.B: «¡Yo soy José!», les dijo a sus hermanos. «¿De verdad vive todavía mi padre?». Sus hermanos estaban tan turbados de verse delante de él que no pudieron decir ni una palabra.
es.R: José les dijo a sus hermanos: «¡Soy José! ¿Todavía vive mi padre?». Pero sus hermanos no podían decir nada. Le tenían demasiado miedo.

fr.L: Et Joseph dit à ses frères : « Moi, [je suis] Joseph ! Mon père vit-il encore ? » Mais ses frères ne purent lui répondre, car ils étaient terrifiés devant lui.
fr.B: « C’est moi, Joseph ! dit-il à ses frères. Mon père est-il vraiment encore en vie ? » Ses frères étaient trop bouleversés pour dire un mot, effrayés de se trouver devant lui.
fr.R: Joseph a dit à ses frères : « Je suis Joseph ! Est-ce que mon père est toujours vivant ? » Mais ses frères ne pouvaient rien dire. Ils avaient trop peur de lui.

sw.L: Yusufu akawaambia ndugu zake, "Mimi [ni] Yusufu! Je, baba yangu bado yu hai?" Lakini ndugu zake hawakuweza kumjibu, kwa maana walifadhaika mbele yake.
sw.B: "Mimi ni Yusufu!" akawaambia ndugu zake. "Je, kweli baba yangu bado yu hai?" Ndugu zake walishtuka mno hata hawakuweza kusema neno lolote, wakiwa wamesimama mbele yake kwa hofu.
sw.R: Yusufu akawaambia ndugu zake, "Mimi ni Yusufu! Je, baba yangu bado anaishi?" Lakini ndugu zake hawakuweza kusema kitu. Walikuwa wanamwogopa sana.

decisions.choice: I am Joseph: the turning point
decisions.reason: Two Hebrew words undo twenty years of hiding. The brothers now stand before the brother they sold, who holds their lives in his hand.

decisions.choice: is my father still alive?: a question from the heart
decisions.reason: Joseph had already been told his father was alive (43:27-28). Now, speaking as a son, he asks again: "my father", not "your father".

decisions.choice: terrified: shaken, dismayed
decisions.reason: Bahal is sudden alarm or dismay. They fear what Joseph may do to them.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֧ף אֶל־אֶחָ֛יו גְּשׁוּ־נָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וַיִּגָּ֑שׁוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֲנִי֙ יוֹסֵ֣ף אֲחִיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־מְכַרְתֶּ֥ם אֹתִ֖י מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joseph to his brothers, draw near, please, to me; and they drew near. And he said, I [am] Joseph your brother, whom you sold to Egypt.

en.L: And Joseph said to his brothers, "Please come near to me." And they came near. And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
en.B: Then Joseph said to his brothers, "Please, come closer." When they had come closer, he said, "I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
en.R: Then Joseph said to them, "Please come close to me." When they did, he said, "I am your brother Joseph. I am the one you sold as a slave to be taken to Egypt.

es.L: Y dijo José a sus hermanos: «{{plural_you:Acérquense|Acercaos}} a mí, por favor». Y se acercaron. Y dijo: «Yo [soy] José, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} hermano, a quien {{plural_you:vendieron|vendisteis}} para Egipto.
es.B: Entonces José les dijo a sus hermanos: «Por favor, {{plural_you:acérquense|acercaos}}». Cuando se acercaron, les dijo: «Soy José, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} hermano, el mismo al que {{plural_you:vendieron|vendisteis}} y fue llevado a Egipto.
es.R: Entonces José les dijo: «Por favor, {{plural_you:acérquense|acercaos}} a mí». Cuando se acercaron, les dijo: «Soy José, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} hermano. Yo soy aquel a quien {{plural_you:vendieron|vendisteis}} como esclavo para que me llevaran a Egipto.

fr.L: Et Joseph dit à ses frères : « Approchez-vous de moi, je vous prie. » Et ils s’approchèrent. Et il dit : « Moi, [je suis] Joseph, votre frère, que vous avez vendu [pour être emmené] en Égypte.
fr.B: Alors Joseph dit à ses frères : « Approchez donc. » Quand ils se furent approchés, il dit : « Je suis Joseph, votre frère, celui que vous avez vendu et qu’on a emmené en Égypte.
fr.R: Ensuite Joseph leur a dit : « S’il vous plaît, venez près de moi. » Quand ils se sont approchés, il a dit : « Je suis votre frère Joseph. C’est moi que vous avez vendu comme esclave pour qu’on m’emmène en Égypte.

sw.L: Yusufu akawaambia ndugu zake, "Tafadhali, sogeeni karibu nami." Nao wakasogea karibu. Akasema, "Mimi [ni] Yusufu ndugu yenu, ambaye mliniuza [nipelekwe] Misri.
sw.B: Kisha Yusufu akawaambia ndugu zake, "Tafadhali, sogeeni karibu." Walipokwisha kusogea, akasema, "Mimi ni ndugu yenu Yusufu, yule mliyemuuza akapelekwa Misri.
sw.R: Kisha Yusufu akawaambia, "Tafadhali njooni karibu nami." Walipokuja karibu, akasema, "Mimi ni ndugu yenu Yusufu. Ni mimi mliyeniuza kama mtumwa, nikapelekwa Misri.

decisions.choice: your brother, whom you sold: the truth named plainly
decisions.reason: Joseph does not hide what they did, but he calls himself their brother first.

decisions.choice: sold as a slave
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sale meant; "slave" stays, as the style guide keeps it for Joseph sold as a slave (37:27-28).

decisions.choice: "que vous avez vendu [pour être emmené] en Égypte"
decisions.reason: French "vendre en Égypte" would say the sale took place in Egypt. The Hebrew "to Egypt" means sold to be taken there, so Literal supplies the movement in brackets.

decisions.choice: "mliniuza [nipelekwe] Misri"
decisions.reason: "Mliniuza Misri" would read as "you sold me in Egypt"; Literal supplies "nipelekwe" ("to be taken") for the Hebrew "to Egypt".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀אַל־תֵּעָ֣צְב֗וּ וְאַל־יִ֨חַר֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־מְכַרְתֶּ֥ם אֹתִ֖י הֵ֑נָּה כִּ֣י לְמִֽחְיָ֔ה שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִפְנֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, do not be grieved, and let it not burn in your eyes that you sold me here; for for preservation of life God sent me before you.

en.L: And now do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you to preserve life.
en.B: But now, do not be upset, and do not be angry with yourselves for selling me here. It was God who sent me on ahead of you, to keep people alive.
en.R: But do not be upset or blame yourselves for selling me. God sent me here ahead of you to save people's lives.

es.L: Y ahora, no {{plural_you:se aflijan|os aflijáis}} ni {{plural_you:se enojen consigo mismos|os enojéis con vosotros mismos}} por haberme vendido aquí, porque para preservar la vida me envió Dios delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Pero ahora no {{plural_you:se angustien|os angustiéis}} ni {{plural_you:se reprochen|os reprochéis}} el haberme vendido aquí. Fue Dios quien me envió por delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} para salvar vidas.
es.R: Pero no {{plural_you:estén tristes|estéis tristes}} ni {{plural_you:se echen la culpa|os echéis la culpa}} por haberme vendido. Dios me mandó aquí antes que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} para salvar la vida de mucha gente.

fr.L: Et maintenant, ne soyez pas affligés et ne soyez pas en colère contre vous-mêmes de m’avoir vendu ici, car c’est pour préserver la vie que Dieu m’a envoyé devant vous.
fr.B: Mais maintenant, ne vous tourmentez pas et ne vous reprochez pas de m’avoir vendu pour que je vienne ici. C’est Dieu qui m’a envoyé en avant de vous, afin de garder des gens en vie.
fr.R: Mais ne soyez pas tristes, et ne vous en voulez pas de m’avoir vendu. Dieu m’a envoyé ici avant vous pour sauver la vie de beaucoup de gens.

sw.L: Na sasa msihuzunike, wala msijikasirikie kwa sababu mliniuza huku, kwa maana ni kwa kuhifadhi uhai Mungu alinituma mbele yenu.
sw.B: Lakini sasa msisikitike, wala msijilaumu kwa kuniuza huku. Mungu ndiye aliyenituma niwatangulie, ili watu waendelee kuishi.
sw.R: Lakini msihuzunike wala msijilaumu kwa kuniuza. Mungu alinituma huku kabla yenu ili niokoe maisha ya watu wengi.

decisions.choice: let it not burn in your eyes: do not be angry with yourselves
decisions.reason: Anger was pictured as burning. Here it is anger turned inward, self-reproach.

decisions.choice: God sent me to preserve life: God's purpose through human wrong
decisions.reason: Joseph does not deny the brothers sold him, but he sees God at work through their deed to keep many alive. He says it three times (verses 5, 7, 8) and again in 50:20. Psalm 105:17 says the same: God "sent a man before them".

decisions.choice: preservation of life: keeping people alive
decisions.reason: Michyah means the preserving of life, and so also the means to live, food (Judges 6:4). The famine context gives both senses.

source.text: כִּי־זֶ֛ה שְׁנָתַ֥יִם הָרָעָ֖ב בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְעוֹד֙ חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־חָרִ֖ישׁ וְקָצִּֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: For this two years [has been] the famine in [the] midst of the land, and still five years [in] which [there will be] no plowing and harvest.

en.L: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are still five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
en.B: The famine has now gripped the land for two years, and for five more years there will be no plowing and no harvest.
en.R: There has been famine in the land for two years now. For five more years, no one will plow fields or gather crops.

es.L: Porque hace ya dos años que hay hambre en medio de la tierra, y aún quedan cinco años en que no habrá ni arada ni siega.
es.B: El hambre azota la tierra desde hace dos años, y durante otros cinco no se podrá arar ni cosechar.
es.R: Ya hace dos años que hay hambre en la región. Durante cinco años más, nadie va a arar los campos ni a recoger cosechas.

fr.L: Car voici deux ans que la famine est au milieu du pays, et il y a encore cinq années où il n’y aura ni labour ni moisson.
fr.B: Cela fait maintenant deux ans que la famine frappe le pays, et pendant cinq ans encore il n’y aura ni labours ni moissons.
fr.R: Il y a déjà deux ans que la famine est dans le pays. Pendant encore cinq ans, personne ne pourra labourer les champs ni faire de récoltes.

sw.L: Kwa maana miaka hii miwili njaa imekuwa katikati ya nchi, na bado iko miaka mitano ambayo hakutakuwa na kulima wala kuvuna.
sw.B: Njaa imeikumba nchi kwa miaka miwili sasa, na kwa miaka mitano mingine hakutakuwa na kulima wala kuvuna.
sw.R: Sasa ni miaka miwili tangu njaa ianze katika nchi. Kwa miaka mitano zaidi, hakuna mtu atakayelima mashamba wala kuvuna mazao.

decisions.choice: plowing and harvest: the whole farming year
decisions.reason: The two words cover the farming year from start to finish: with no rain or flood, nothing is sown and nothing reaped.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֤נִי אֱלֹהִים֙ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם לָשׂ֥וּם לָכֶ֛ם שְׁאֵרִ֖ית בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּלְהַחֲי֣וֹת לָכֶ֔ם לִפְלֵיטָ֖ה גְּדֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent me God before you to make for you a remnant on the earth and to keep alive for you for a great deliverance.

en.L: And God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth, and to keep you alive by a great deliverance.
en.B: God sent me ahead of you to make sure your family would survive on the earth, and to save your lives in a great act of rescue.
en.R: God sent me ahead of you to keep your family alive on the earth. He did it to save you in a wonderful way.

es.L: Y Dios me envió delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} para {{plural_you:asegurarles|aseguraros}} un remanente en la tierra, y para {{plural_you:mantenerlos|manteneros}} con vida mediante una gran liberación.
es.B: Dios me envió por delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} para que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} familia sobreviviera en la tierra, y para {{plural_you:salvarles|salvaros}} la vida con un gran rescate.
es.R: Dios me mandó antes que a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} para que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} familia siga viva en la tierra. Lo hizo para {{plural_you:salvarlos|salvaros}} de una manera maravillosa.

fr.L: Et Dieu m’a envoyé devant vous pour vous assurer un reste sur la terre, et pour vous garder en vie par une grande délivrance.
fr.B: Dieu m’a envoyé en avant de vous pour que votre famille survive sur la terre, et pour vous sauver la vie par une délivrance éclatante.
fr.R: Dieu m’a envoyé avant vous pour que votre famille reste en vie sur la terre. Il l’a fait pour vous sauver d’une manière extraordinaire.

sw.L: Mungu alinituma mbele yenu ili kuwawekea mabaki duniani, na kuwahifadhi hai kwa wokovu mkuu.
sw.B: Mungu alinituma niwatangulie ili jamaa yenu iendelee kuwepo duniani, na kuyaokoa maisha yenu kwa uokoaji mkubwa.
sw.R: Mungu alinituma huku kabla yenu ili jamaa yenu iendelee kuishi duniani. Alifanya hivyo ili awaokoe kwa njia ya ajabu.

decisions.choice: remnant: those who survive
decisions.reason: She'erit is what remains after disaster, the survivors who carry on a family or people. The prophets later use the word for the faithful remnant of Israel (Isaiah 10:20-22).

decisions.choice: for a great deliverance: by a great rescue
alternatives: as a great company of survivors
decisions.reason: Peletah can mean an escape or rescue, or the band of those who escape. "To keep you alive by a great deliverance" is the more natural reading; "to keep alive for you many survivors" is possible.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה לֹֽא־אַתֶּ֞ם שְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם אֹתִי֙ הֵ֔נָּה כִּ֖י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְשִׂימֵ֨נִֽי לְאָ֜ב לְפַרְעֹ֗ה וּלְאָדוֹן֙ לְכָל־בֵּית֔וֹ וּמֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, not you sent me here, but God; and he has made me a father to Pharaoh and lord of all his house and ruler over all [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: So now it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
en.B: So it was not really you who sent me here, but God. And he has made me a father to Pharaoh, master of his whole household and ruler of all Egypt.
en.R: So it was not really you who sent me here. It was God. He has made me Pharaoh's most trusted adviser. I am in charge of his whole palace, and I rule over all of Egypt.

es.L: Así que ahora, no fueron {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quienes me {{plural_you:enviaron|enviasteis}} aquí, sino Dios; y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me ha puesto por padre del faraón, y señor de toda su casa, y gobernador de toda la tierra de Egipto.
es.B: Así que en realidad no fueron {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quienes me {{plural_you:enviaron|enviasteis}} aquí, sino Dios. Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me ha hecho padre del faraón, señor de toda su casa y gobernante de todo Egipto.
es.R: Así que en realidad no fueron {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que me {{plural_you:mandaron|mandasteis}} aquí. Fue Dios. Él me ha hecho el consejero de más confianza del faraón. Estoy a cargo de todo su palacio, y gobierno todo Egipto.

fr.L: Et maintenant, ce n’est pas vous qui m’avez envoyé ici, mais Dieu ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a établi père pour Pharaon, seigneur de toute sa maison et gouverneur de tout le pays d’Égypte.
fr.B: Ce n’est donc pas vraiment vous qui m’avez envoyé ici, c’est Dieu. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait de moi un père pour Pharaon, le maître de toute sa maison et le gouverneur de toute l’Égypte.
fr.R: Ce n’est donc pas vraiment vous qui m’avez envoyé ici. C’est Dieu. Il a fait de moi le conseiller le plus proche de Pharaon. Je dirige tout son palais, et je gouverne toute l’Égypte.

sw.L: Basi sasa, si ninyi mlionituma huku, bali Mungu; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} amenifanya kuwa baba kwa Farao, na bwana wa nyumba yake yote, na mtawala juu ya nchi yote ya Misri.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo kwa kweli si ninyi mlionileta huku, bali ni Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} amenifanya kuwa baba kwa Farao, bwana wa watu wote wa nyumba yake, na mtawala wa Misri yote.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo si ninyi hasa mlionileta huku. Ni Mungu. Amenifanya kuwa mshauri wa Farao anayeaminiwa kuliko wote. Mimi ndiye ninayesimamia ikulu yake yote, na ninatawala Misri yote.

decisions.choice: father to Pharaoh: a title of a chief adviser
decisions.reason: "Father" was a title of honor for a trusted counselor (compare Judges 17:10; 2 Kings 6:21). It speaks of trust and authority, not age.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh's most trusted adviser
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title instead of keeping the picture.

decisions.choice: "y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me ha puesto" (L), "Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me ha hecho" (B)
alternatives: "y me ha puesto", with no pronoun
decisions.reason: Spanish keeps an explicit "él" to stress that it is God, not the brothers, who raised Joseph; as a pronoun for God it takes the deity pronoun setting. At Readable it opens the sentence and is capitalised either way.

decisions.choice: "et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a établi" (L), "Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait de moi" (B)
alternatives: no span, as in the English "he has made me"
decisions.reason: "Il" here stands for God in mid-sentence, so it takes the deity pronoun setting, as the French style guide asks for every pronoun for God. At Readable "Il" opens the sentence and is written plainly.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} amenifanya"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced join the clause with "naye" ("and he"), a free pronoun for God, which takes the deity pronoun setting. Readable starts a new sentence with the verb alone, so it has no span.

source.text: מַהֲרוּ֮ וַעֲל֣וּ אֶל־אָבִי֒ וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ בִּנְךָ֣ יוֹסֵ֔ף שָׂמַ֧נִי אֱלֹהִ֛ים לְאָד֖וֹן לְכָל־מִצְרָ֑יִם רְדָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Hurry and go up to my father and you will say to him, thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me, do not delay.

en.L: Hurry and go up to my father and say to him, 'Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.
en.B: Go up to my father quickly and tell him, 'This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me master of all Egypt. Come down to me without wasting any time.
en.R: Now hurry back to my father. Tell him, 'Your son Joseph says: God has made me ruler of all Egypt. Come down to me right away.

es.L: {{plural_you:Dense prisa|Daos prisa}} y {{plural_you:suban|subid}} a mi padre, y {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: “Así dice tu hijo José: Dios me ha puesto por señor de todo Egipto; baja a mí, no te detengas.
es.B: {{plural_you:Suban|Subid}} pronto adonde está mi padre y {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: “Esto dice tu hijo José: Dios me ha hecho señor de todo Egipto. Ven a mí sin perder tiempo.
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} rápido a casa de mi padre. {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}}: “Tu hijo José te manda decir: Dios me ha hecho gobernador de todo Egipto. Ven aquí conmigo enseguida.

fr.L: Hâtez-vous et montez vers mon père, et vous lui direz : “Ainsi dit ton fils Joseph : Dieu m’a établi seigneur de toute l’Égypte. Descends vers moi, ne tarde pas.
fr.B: Remontez vite chez mon père et dites-lui : “Voici ce que dit ton fils Joseph : Dieu a fait de moi le maître de toute l’Égypte. Descends me rejoindre sans perdre de temps.
fr.R: Maintenant, retournez vite chez mon père. Dites-lui : “Ton fils Joseph te fait dire : Dieu a fait de moi le chef de toute l’Égypte. Viens vite me rejoindre.

sw.L: Fanyeni haraka mpande kwa baba yangu, mkamwambie, 'Hivi ndivyo asemavyo mwanao Yusufu: Mungu amenifanya kuwa bwana wa Misri yote; shuka kwangu, usikawie.
sw.B: Pandeni upesi kwa baba yangu mkamwambie, 'Mwanao Yusufu anasema hivi: Mungu amenifanya kuwa bwana wa Misri yote. Shuka uje kwangu bila kukawia.
sw.R: Sasa rudini haraka kwa baba yangu. Mwambieni, 'Mwanao Yusufu anasema: Mungu amenifanya kuwa mtawala wa Misri yote. Njoo kwangu mara moja.

decisions.choice: thus says: the formula of a messenger
decisions.reason: "Thus says" introduces a message delivered word for word for the sender, the form later used by the prophets ("thus says the LORD").

decisions.choice: God has made me lord: honor credited to God
decisions.reason: Joseph's message names God, not Pharaoh, as the one who raised him.

source.text: וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֣ בְאֶֽרֶץ־גֹּ֗שֶׁן וְהָיִ֤יתָ קָרוֹב֙ אֵלַ֔י אַתָּ֕ה וּבָנֶ֖יךָ וּבְנֵ֣י בָנֶ֑יךָ וְצֹאנְךָ֥ וּבְקָרְךָ֖ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will dwell in [the] land of Goshen and you will be near to me, you and your children and your children's children, and your flocks and your herds and all that [is] to you.

en.L: You shall live in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me, you and your children and your children's children, your flocks and your herds and all that you have.
en.B: You can settle in the region of Goshen and be close to me, you and your children and grandchildren, your sheep and goats and cattle, and everything that belongs to you.
en.R: You can live in the land of Goshen, near me. Bring your children and grandchildren, your sheep, goats and cattle, and everything you own.

es.L: Y habitarás en la tierra de Gosén, y estarás cerca de mí, tú y tus hijos y los hijos de tus hijos, y tus rebaños y tus vacadas y todo lo que tienes.
es.B: Podrás establecerte en la región de Gosén y estar cerca de mí, tú con tus hijos y tus nietos, tus ovejas y cabras, tus vacas y todo lo que te pertenece.
es.R: Podrás vivir en la tierra de Gosén, cerca de mí. Trae a tus hijos y a tus nietos, tus ovejas, tus cabras, tus vacas y todo lo que tienes.

fr.L: Et tu habiteras dans le pays de Goshen, et tu seras près de moi, toi, tes enfants et les enfants de tes enfants, ton petit bétail, ton gros bétail et tout ce qui est à toi.
fr.B: Tu pourras t’installer dans la région de Goshen et être près de moi, toi, tes enfants et tes petits-enfants, tes moutons et tes chèvres, tes bœufs, et tout ce qui t’appartient.
fr.R: Tu pourras vivre dans la région de Goshen, près de moi. Amène tes enfants et tes petits-enfants, tes moutons, tes chèvres, tes bœufs et tout ce que tu possèdes.

sw.L: Nawe utakaa katika nchi ya Gosheni, nawe utakuwa karibu nami, wewe na watoto wako na watoto wa watoto wako, na makundi yako ya kondoo na makundi yako ya ng'ombe na vyote ulivyo navyo.
sw.B: Utaweza kukaa katika eneo la Gosheni, karibu nami, wewe na watoto wako na wajukuu wako, kondoo na mbuzi wako, ng'ombe wako, na kila kitu ulicho nacho.
sw.R: Utaweza kuishi katika nchi ya Gosheni, karibu nami. Waje pamoja nawe watoto wako na wajukuu wako, pamoja na kondoo, mbuzi na ng'ombe wako, na vyote ulivyo navyo.

decisions.choice: Goshen: grazing land in the eastern Nile Delta
decisions.reason: Goshen lay in the northeast of Egypt, in the delta near the route to Canaan. It was good land for flocks and close to Joseph's seat of government.

decisions.choice: sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Tson means a flock of small animals, sheep and goats together.

source.text: וְכִלְכַּלְתִּ֤י אֹֽתְךָ֙ שָׁ֔ם כִּי־ע֛וֹד חָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים רָעָ֑ב פֶּן־תִּוָּרֵ֛שׁ אַתָּ֥ה וּבֵֽיתְךָ֖ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will provide for you there, for still five years [of] famine, lest you become impoverished, you and your household and all that [is] to you.

en.L: And I will provide for you there, for there are still five years of famine to come, so that you and your household and all that you have do not come to poverty.'
en.B: I will supply your needs there, since there are still five years of famine ahead. Otherwise you, your family and all you have will end up in want.'
en.R: I will take care of you there. There will be five more years of famine, and I do not want you, your family and your animals to go hungry.'

es.L: Y allí te sustentaré, porque aún [quedan] cinco años de hambre, para que no caigas en la pobreza, tú y tu casa y todo lo que tienes”.
es.B: Allí yo me encargaré de que no te falte nada, porque todavía quedan cinco años de hambre. De lo contrario, tú, tu familia y todo lo tuyo acabarían en la miseria”.
es.R: Allí yo te cuidaré. Todavía va a haber cinco años más de hambre, y no quiero que tú, tu familia y tus animales pasen hambre”.

fr.L: Et là je pourvoirai à tes besoins, car il y aura encore cinq années de famine, de peur que tu ne tombes dans la misère, toi, ta maison et tout ce qui est à toi.”
fr.B: Là, je subviendrai à tes besoins, car il reste encore cinq années de famine. Sinon, toi, ta famille et tout ce que tu as, vous finiriez dans le dénuement.”
fr.R: Là-bas, je prendrai soin de toi. Il y aura encore cinq ans de famine, et je ne veux pas que toi, ta famille et tes animaux, vous manquiez de nourriture.”

sw.L: Nami nitakutunza huko, kwa maana bado kuna miaka mitano ya njaa, usije ukafilisika, wewe na nyumba yako na vyote ulivyo navyo.'
sw.B: Nitakupatia mahitaji yako huko, kwa kuwa bado kuna miaka mitano ya njaa mbele. La sivyo, wewe, jamaa yako na vyote ulivyo navyo mtaishia katika uhitaji.'
sw.R: Nitakutunza huko. Kutakuwa na miaka mitano zaidi ya njaa, na sitaki wewe, jamaa yako na wanyama wako mkose chakula.'

decisions.choice: become impoverished: lose everything
decisions.reason: The verb means to be dispossessed or reduced to poverty.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֤ה עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ רֹא֔וֹת וְעֵינֵ֖י אָחִ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ין כִּי־פִ֖י הַֽמְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And here, your eyes [are] seeing and [the] eyes of my brother Benjamin, that my mouth [is] the [one] speaking to you.

en.L: And look, your eyes and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
en.B: You can see for yourselves, and so can my brother Benjamin, that it is really I who am speaking to you.
en.R: You can see with your own eyes, and so can my brother Benjamin, that it is really me, Joseph, talking to you.

es.L: Y he aquí, {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} ojos ven, y los ojos de mi hermano Benjamín, que [es] mi boca la que {{plural_you:les|os}} habla.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes mismos pueden|Vosotros mismos podéis}} verlo, y también mi hermano Benjamín: soy yo de verdad quien {{plural_you:les|os}} habla.
es.R: {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} verlo con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios ojos, y también mi hermano Benjamín: de verdad soy yo, José, el que {{plural_you:les|os}} está hablando.

fr.L: Et voici, vos yeux voient, ainsi que les yeux de mon frère Benjamin, que c’est ma bouche qui vous parle.
fr.B: Vous le voyez bien vous-mêmes, et mon frère Benjamin aussi : c’est vraiment moi qui vous parle.
fr.R: Vous pouvez le voir de vos propres yeux, et mon frère Benjamin aussi : c’est vraiment moi, Joseph, qui vous parle.

sw.L: Na tazama, macho yenu yanaona, na macho ya ndugu yangu Benyamini, kwamba ni kinywa changu kinachosema nanyi.
sw.B: Mnaweza kuona wenyewe, naye ndugu yangu Benyamini anaona, kwamba ni mimi hasa ninayesema nanyi.
sw.R: Mnaona kwa macho yenu wenyewe, na ndugu yangu Benyamini naye anaona, kwamba kweli ni mimi, Yusufu, ninayeongea nanyi.

decisions.choice: my mouth speaks to you: no longer through an interpreter
decisions.reason: Until now Joseph had spoken to them through an interpreter (42:23). Now he speaks their own language directly, proof of who he is.

source.text: וְהִגַּדְתֶּ֣ם לְאָבִ֗י אֶת־כָּל־כְּבוֹדִי֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר רְאִיתֶ֑ם וּמִֽהַרְתֶּ֛ם וְהוֹרַדְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־אָבִ֖י הֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will tell my father all my honor in Egypt and all that you have seen; and you will hurry and bring down my father here.

en.L: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt and of all that you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here."
en.B: Tell my father about all the honor I have in Egypt and everything you have seen. And hurry, bring my father down here."
en.R: Tell my father how important I am in Egypt. Tell him everything you have seen. Then hurry and bring my father here."

es.L: Y {{plural_you:contarán|contaréis}} a mi padre toda mi gloria en Egipto y todo lo que {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}}. {{plural_you:Apresúrense|Apresuraos}} y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} bajar aquí a mi padre».
es.B: {{plural_you:Cuéntenle|Contadle}} a mi padre todo el honor que tengo en Egipto y todo lo que {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}}. ¡Y {{plural_you:dense prisa|daos prisa}}, {{plural_you:traigan|traed}} aquí a mi padre!».
es.R: {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}} a mi padre lo importante que soy en Egipto. {{plural_you:Cuéntenle|Contadle}} todo lo que {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}}. Luego {{plural_you:dense prisa|daos prisa}} y {{plural_you:tráiganlo|traedlo}} aquí».

fr.L: Vous raconterez à mon père toute ma gloire en Égypte et tout ce que vous avez vu. Hâtez-vous de faire descendre mon père ici. »
fr.B: Racontez à mon père tout l’honneur dont je jouis en Égypte et tout ce que vous avez vu. Et faites vite, amenez mon père ici. »
fr.R: Dites à mon père combien je suis important en Égypte. Racontez-lui tout ce que vous avez vu. Puis dépêchez-vous de l’amener ici. »

sw.L: Nanyi mtamweleza baba yangu habari za utukufu wangu wote katika Misri, na yote mliyoyaona. Fanyeni haraka mkamlete baba yangu huku."
sw.B: Mwelezeni baba yangu juu ya heshima yote niliyo nayo katika Misri, na kila kitu mlichokiona. Tena fanyeni haraka, mleteni baba yangu huku."
sw.R: Mwambieni baba yangu jinsi nilivyo mtu mkubwa katika Misri. Mwelezeni yote mliyoyaona. Kisha fanyeni haraka mmlete baba yangu huku."

decisions.choice: my honor: my high standing
decisions.reason: Kavod is weight, and so importance, honor and splendor. Here it is Joseph's rank and wealth in Egypt.

source.text: וַיִּפֹּ֛ל עַל־צַוְּארֵ֥י בִנְיָמִֽן־אָחִ֖יו וַיֵּ֑בְךְּ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן בָּכָ֖ה עַל־צַוָּארָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he fell on [the] neck of Benjamin his brother and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.

en.L: And he fell on his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
en.B: Then he threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept as he embraced him.
en.R: Then Joseph hugged his brother Benjamin and cried. Benjamin cried too as he hugged Joseph.

es.L: Y se echó sobre el cuello de su hermano Benjamín y lloró, y Benjamín lloró sobre su cuello.
es.B: Entonces abrazó a su hermano Benjamín y se echó a llorar, y Benjamín también lloró abrazado a él.
es.R: Entonces José abrazó a su hermano Benjamín y lloró. Benjamín también lloró mientras abrazaba a José.

fr.L: Et il tomba au cou de son frère Benjamin et pleura, et Benjamin pleura à son cou.
fr.B: Puis il serra dans ses bras son frère Benjamin et pleura, et Benjamin pleura aussi en l’étreignant.
fr.R: Ensuite Joseph a pris son frère Benjamin dans ses bras et il a pleuré. Benjamin aussi a pleuré en serrant Joseph dans ses bras.

sw.L: Akaangukia shingo ya ndugu yake Benyamini, akalia; naye Benyamini akalia shingoni mwake.
sw.B: Kisha akamkumbatia ndugu yake Benyamini akalia, naye Benyamini akalia huku akimkumbatia.
sw.R: Kisha Yusufu akamkumbatia ndugu yake Benyamini, akalia. Benyamini naye akalia huku akimkumbatia Yusufu.

decisions.choice: fell on his neck: embraced him
decisions.reason: To fall on someone's neck is to throw one's arms around him (33:4; 46:29).

source.text: וַיְנַשֵּׁ֥ק לְכָל־אֶחָ֖יו וַיֵּ֣בְךְּ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן דִּבְּר֥וּ אֶחָ֖יו אִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them; and after that his brothers spoke with him.

en.L: And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them. After that his brothers talked with him.
en.B: He kissed each of his brothers and wept as he held them. Only then were his brothers able to talk with him.
en.R: Then he kissed all his brothers and cried as he hugged them. After that, his brothers began talking with him.

es.L: Y besó a todos sus hermanos y lloró sobre ellos; y después de eso sus hermanos hablaron con él.
es.B: Besó a cada uno de sus hermanos y lloró abrazándolos. Solo entonces sus hermanos pudieron hablar con él.
es.R: Luego besó a todos sus hermanos y lloró mientras los abrazaba. Después de eso, sus hermanos empezaron a hablar con él.

fr.L: Et il embrassa tous ses frères et pleura sur eux. Après cela, ses frères parlèrent avec lui.
fr.B: Il embrassa chacun de ses frères et pleura en les tenant serrés contre lui. Alors seulement ses frères purent parler avec lui.
fr.R: Ensuite il a embrassé tous ses frères et il a pleuré en les serrant dans ses bras. Après cela, ses frères ont commencé à lui parler.

sw.L: Akawabusu ndugu zake wote, akalia juu yao; na baada ya hayo ndugu zake wakazungumza naye.
sw.B: Akambusu kila mmoja wa ndugu zake na kulia akiwakumbatia. Ndipo ndugu zake walipoweza kuzungumza naye.
sw.R: Kisha akawabusu ndugu zake wote, akalia huku akiwakumbatia. Baada ya hapo, ndugu zake wakaanza kuongea naye.

decisions.choice: his brothers spoke with him: a broken silence healed
decisions.reason: Years before, the brothers "could not speak peaceably to him" (37:4). Now they talk with him.

source.text: וְהַקֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמַ֗ע בֵּ֤ית פַּרְעֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֖אוּ אֲחֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וּבְעֵינֵ֖י עֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And the report was heard [in the] house of Pharaoh, saying, have come [the] brothers of Joseph; and it was good in [the] eyes of Pharaoh and in [the] eyes of his servants.

en.L: And the report was heard in Pharaoh's house, "Joseph's brothers have come," and it pleased Pharaoh and his officials.
en.B: News reached Pharaoh's palace that Joseph's brothers had arrived, and Pharaoh and his officials were glad.
en.R: The news spread to Pharaoh's palace: "Joseph's brothers have come!" Pharaoh and his officials were happy to hear it.

es.L: Y se oyó la noticia en la casa del faraón: «Han venido los hermanos de José», y esto pareció bien al faraón y a sus oficiales.
es.B: Al palacio del faraón llegó la noticia de que los hermanos de José habían venido, y el faraón y sus oficiales se alegraron.
es.R: La noticia corrió hasta el palacio del faraón: «¡Han venido los hermanos de José!». Al faraón y a sus oficiales les alegró mucho oírlo.

fr.L: Et la nouvelle se fit entendre dans la maison de Pharaon : « Les frères de Joseph sont venus », et cela plut à Pharaon et à ses officiers.
fr.B: La nouvelle parvint au palais de Pharaon : les frères de Joseph étaient arrivés. Pharaon et ses officiers s’en réjouirent.
fr.R: La nouvelle s’est répandue jusqu’au palais de Pharaon : « Les frères de Joseph sont venus ! » Pharaon et ses officiers ont été contents de l’apprendre.

sw.L: Na habari ikasikika katika nyumba ya Farao, kwamba, "Ndugu zake Yusufu wamekuja," ikawa njema machoni pa Farao na machoni pa maafisa wake.
sw.B: Habari zilifika ikulu ya Farao kwamba ndugu zake Yusufu wamefika, naye Farao na maafisa wake wakafurahi.
sw.R: Habari zikaenea hadi ikulu ya Farao: "Ndugu zake Yusufu wamekuja!" Farao na maafisa wake walifurahi kusikia hivyo.

decisions.choice: it was good in the eyes of: it pleased
decisions.reason: A common idiom for approval.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are his court, his high officials.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֱמֹ֥ר אֶל־אַחֶ֖יךָ זֹ֣את עֲשׂ֑וּ טַֽעֲנוּ֙ אֶת־בְּעִ֣ירְכֶ֔ם וּלְכוּ־בֹ֖אוּ אַ֥רְצָה כְּנָֽעַן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Pharaoh to Joseph, say to your brothers, this do: load your animals and go, come to [the] land of Canaan,

en.L: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Say to your brothers, 'Do this: load your animals and go back to the land of Canaan,
en.B: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers to load up their animals and return to the land of Canaan.
en.R: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and go back to Canaan.

es.L: Y dijo el faraón a José: «Di a tus hermanos: “{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} esto: {{plural_you:carguen|cargad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} bestias y {{plural_you:vayan|id}}, {{plural_you:regresen|regresad}} a la tierra de Canaán,
es.B: El faraón le dijo a José: «Diles a tus hermanos que carguen sus animales y vuelvan a la tierra de Canaán.
es.R: El faraón le dijo a José: «Diles a tus hermanos que carguen sus burros y regresen a Canaán.

fr.L: Et Pharaon dit à Joseph : « Dis à tes frères : “Faites ceci : chargez vos bêtes et partez, retournez au pays de Canaan,
fr.B: Pharaon dit à Joseph : « Dis à tes frères de charger leurs bêtes et de retourner au pays de Canaan.
fr.R: Pharaon a dit à Joseph : « Dis à tes frères de charger leurs ânes et de rentrer en Canaan.

sw.L: Farao akamwambia Yusufu, "Waambie ndugu zako, 'Fanyeni hivi: pakieni wanyama wenu mizigo, mwende, mrudi katika nchi ya Kanaani,
sw.B: Farao akamwambia Yusufu, "Waambie ndugu zako wapakie wanyama wao mizigo, warudi katika nchi ya Kanaani.
sw.R: Farao akamwambia Yusufu, "Waambie ndugu zako wapakie punda wao mizigo, warudi Kanaani.

decisions.choice: indirect speech
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn Pharaoh's message into reported instructions to avoid quotations within quotations; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: donkeys
decisions.reason: Be'ir means pack animals or livestock; the brothers' animals were donkeys (44:3, 13).

source.text: וּקְח֧וּ אֶת־אֲבִיכֶ֛ם וְאֶת־בָּתֵּיכֶ֖ם וּבֹ֣אוּ אֵלָ֑י וְאֶתְּנָ֣ה לָכֶ֗ם אֶת־טוּב֙ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וְאִכְל֖וּ אֶת־חֵ֥לֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: and fetch your father and your households and come to me; and I will give to you [the] good of [the] land of Egypt, and you will eat [the] fat of the land.

en.L: and take your father and your households and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.'
en.B: They are to bring their father and their families and come to me. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they will live off the richest produce in the country.
en.R: Then they should bring their father and their families back here to me. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they will have plenty of good food to eat.

es.L: y {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} padre y a {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} familias, y {{plural_you:vengan|venid}} a mí, y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} daré lo mejor de la tierra de Egipto, y {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} la grosura de la tierra”.
es.B: Que tomen a su padre y a sus familias y vengan a mí. Yo les daré la mejor tierra de Egipto, y vivirán de los productos más ricos del país.
es.R: Después, que traigan aquí a su padre y a sus familias. Yo les daré la mejor tierra de Egipto, y tendrán mucha comida buena.

fr.L: et prenez votre père et vos familles, et venez vers moi, et je vous donnerai le meilleur du pays d’Égypte, et vous mangerez la graisse du pays.”
fr.B: Qu’ils prennent leur père et leurs familles et qu’ils viennent auprès de moi. Je leur donnerai la meilleure terre d’Égypte, et ils vivront des produits les plus riches du pays.
fr.R: Ensuite, qu’ils ramènent ici leur père et leurs familles. Je leur donnerai la meilleure terre d’Égypte, et ils auront beaucoup de bonne nourriture.

sw.L: mkamchukue baba yenu na jamaa zenu, mje kwangu; nami nitawapa mema ya nchi ya Misri, nanyi mtakula unono wa nchi.'
sw.B: Wamchukue baba yao na jamaa zao waje kwangu. Nitawapa ardhi iliyo bora kuliko zote katika Misri, nao wataishi kwa mazao bora kabisa ya nchi hii.
sw.R: Kisha wamlete baba yao na jamaa zao hapa kwangu. Nitawapa ardhi iliyo bora zaidi katika Misri, nao watakuwa na chakula kizuri kingi.

decisions.choice: the fat of the land: its richest produce
decisions.reason: Fat was the choicest part of an animal, so "the fat of the land" is the best that the land produces.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֥ה צֻוֵּ֖יתָה זֹ֣את עֲשׂ֑וּ קְחוּ־לָכֶם֩ מֵאֶ֨רֶץ מִצְרַ֜יִם עֲגָל֗וֹת לְטַפְּכֶם֙ וְלִנְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם וּנְשָׂאתֶ֥ם אֶת־אֲבִיכֶ֖ם וּבָאתֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, you are commanded: this do: take for yourselves from [the] land of Egypt carts for your little ones and for your wives, and you will carry your father and you will come.

en.L: And you are commanded, 'Do this: take carts from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father and come.
en.B: And you are to give them this order as well: take carts from Egypt for their children and their wives, and bring their father here.
en.R: Tell them also to take wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And they should bring their father here.

es.L: Y a ti se te ordena: “{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} esto: {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} de la tierra de Egipto carros para {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pequeños y para {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} mujeres, y {{plural_you:traigan|traed}} a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} padre y {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}.
es.B: Y tú les darás también esta orden: que tomen carros de Egipto para sus hijos y sus mujeres, y que traigan aquí a su padre.
es.R: Diles también que se lleven carretas de Egipto para que viajen en ellas sus mujeres y sus hijos. Y que traigan aquí a su padre.

fr.L: Et toi, tu reçois cet ordre : “Faites ceci : prenez du pays d’Égypte des chariots pour vos petits enfants et pour vos femmes, et amenez votre père, et venez.
fr.B: Tu leur donneras aussi cet ordre : qu’ils prennent en Égypte des chariots pour leurs enfants et pour leurs femmes, et qu’ils amènent leur père ici.
fr.R: Dis-leur aussi de prendre des chariots en Égypte pour que leurs femmes et leurs enfants voyagent dedans. Et qu’ils amènent leur père ici.

sw.L: Nawe umeamriwa, 'Fanyeni hivi: chukueni magari kutoka nchi ya Misri kwa ajili ya watoto wenu wadogo na wake zenu, mkamchukue baba yenu, mje.
sw.B: Nawe uwape agizo hili pia: wachukue magari kutoka Misri kwa ajili ya watoto wao na wake zao, wamlete baba yao huku.
sw.R: Waambie pia wachukue magari kutoka Misri ili wake zao na watoto wao wapande ndani yake. Na wamlete baba yao huku.

decisions.choice: you are commanded: Pharaoh authorizes Joseph
decisions.reason: Pharaoh tells Joseph that he, Joseph, is authorized to give this order to his brothers. The change from singular to plural in mid-sentence is abrupt, but the sense is clear.

decisions.choice: carts: wheeled wagons
decisions.reason: Agalot were two-wheeled carts pulled by oxen, common in Egypt but rare in the hill country of Canaan. Seeing them convinces Jacob (verse 27).

source.text: וְעֵ֣ינְכֶ֔ם אַל־תָּחֹ֖ס עַל־כְּלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּי־ט֛וּב כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לָכֶ֥ם הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And your eye, let it not pity your belongings; for [the] good of all [the] land of Egypt, to you it [is].

en.L: Do not let your eye regret your possessions, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.'"
en.B: They need not worry about the things they leave behind, because the best of all Egypt will be theirs."
en.R: They should not worry about leaving things behind. The best of everything in Egypt will be theirs."

es.L: Y que no se lamente {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} ojo por {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enseres, porque lo mejor de toda la tierra de Egipto [es] {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}”».
es.B: Que no se preocupen por las cosas que dejen atrás, porque lo mejor de todo Egipto será para ellos».
es.R: No tienen que preocuparse por dejar cosas atrás. Lo mejor de todo Egipto será para ellos».

fr.L: Et que votre œil n’ait pas de regret pour vos affaires, car le meilleur de tout le pays d’Égypte est à vous.” »
fr.B: Qu’ils ne se soucient pas de ce qu’ils laisseront derrière eux, car le meilleur de toute l’Égypte sera à eux. »
fr.R: Ils ne doivent pas s’inquiéter de laisser des choses derrière eux. Ce qu’il y a de meilleur en Égypte sera à eux. »

sw.L: Na jicho lenu lisione huruma kwa vitu vyenu, kwa maana mema ya nchi yote ya Misri ni yenu.'"
sw.B: Wasihangaike juu ya vitu watakavyoviacha nyuma, kwa sababu vitu bora vya Misri yote vitakuwa vyao."
sw.R: Wasiwe na wasiwasi kuhusu kuacha vitu vyao nyuma. Vitu vizuri kuliko vyote katika Misri vitakuwa vyao."

decisions.choice: let your eye not pity your things: do not mind leaving them
decisions.reason: The eye that "pities" looks back with regret. Pharaoh tells them not to be concerned for the goods they must leave in Canaan.

source.text: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֥ם יוֹסֵ֛ף עֲגָל֖וֹת עַל־פִּ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֛ם צֵדָ֖ה לַדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And did so [the] sons of Israel; and gave to them Joseph carts according to [the] mouth of Pharaoh, and he gave to them provisions for the way.

en.L: And the sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them carts, as Pharaoh had commanded, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
en.B: The sons of Israel did as they were told. Joseph gave them carts at Pharaoh's command, and supplies for the road.
en.R: So Jacob's sons did this. Joseph gave them wagons, as Pharaoh had ordered, and food for the trip.

es.L: Y así lo hicieron los hijos de Israel; y José les dio carros según lo que había ordenado el faraón, y les dio provisiones para el camino.
es.B: Los hijos de Israel hicieron lo que se les había dicho. José les dio carros por orden del faraón, y provisiones para el camino.
es.R: Así que los hijos de Jacob lo hicieron. José les dio carretas, como había ordenado el faraón, y comida para el viaje.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Israël firent ainsi. Joseph leur donna des chariots sur l’ordre de Pharaon, et il leur donna des provisions pour la route.
fr.B: Les fils d’Israël firent ce qu’on leur avait dit. Joseph leur donna des chariots, sur l’ordre de Pharaon, et des vivres pour la route.
fr.R: Les fils de Jacob ont donc fait ce qu’on leur avait dit. Joseph leur a donné des chariots, comme Pharaon l’avait ordonné, et de la nourriture pour le voyage.

sw.L: Wana wa Israeli wakafanya hivyo; Yusufu akawapa magari kwa amri ya Farao, akawapa na mahitaji ya safari.
sw.B: Wana wa Israeli wakafanya kama walivyoambiwa. Yusufu akawapa magari kwa agizo la Farao, pamoja na mahitaji ya njiani.
sw.R: Basi wana wa Yakobo wakafanya hivyo. Yusufu akawapa magari, kama Farao alivyoagiza, na chakula cha safari.

decisions.choice: according to the mouth of Pharaoh: at Pharaoh's command
decisions.reason: The "mouth" stands for what someone says or orders.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: Israel is Jacob's God-given name (32:28). The phrase that becomes the name of the people still means Jacob's own sons here.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" at Balanced
alternatives: "los israelitas", the Pentateuch's usual Balanced wording
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means Jacob's own sons, not yet the people, so Balanced keeps "los hijos de Israel" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "les fils d'Israël", with no gender setting
alternatives: "les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d'Israël" (L) and "les {{gender:Israélites|fils d'Israël}}" (B), the Pentateuch's usual wordings
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means Jacob's own sons, the men who made the journey, not yet the people of Israel, so "fils" is exact and there is no inclusive alternative to offer.

decisions.choice: "wana wa Israeli" at Balanced
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means Jacob's own sons, not yet the people, so Balanced keeps "wana wa Israeli" as the English does.

source.text: לְכֻלָּ֥ם נָתַ֛ן לָאִ֖ישׁ חֲלִפ֣וֹת שְׂמָלֹ֑ת וּלְבִנְיָמִ֤ן נָתַן֙ שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת כֶּ֔סֶף וְחָמֵ֖שׁ חֲלִפֹ֥ת שְׂמָלֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: To all of them he gave, to each man, changes of clothes; and to Benjamin he gave three hundred [of] silver and five changes of clothes.

en.L: To each and every one of them he gave changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave 300 [shekels] of silver and five changes of clothing.
en.B: He gave each of them a new set of clothes, but to Benjamin he gave {{units:about 7.5 pounds|300 shekels}} of silver and five sets of clothes.
en.R: He gave each of his brothers new clothes. But he gave Benjamin five sets of new clothes and {{units:about 7.5 pounds|300 shekels}} of silver.

es.L: A todos ellos dio, a cada uno, mudas de ropa; pero a Benjamín le dio 300 [siclos] de plata y cinco mudas de ropa.
es.B: A cada uno le dio ropa nueva para cambiarse, pero a Benjamín le dio {{units:unos 3,5 kilos|300 siclos}} de plata y cinco mudas de ropa.
es.R: A cada uno de sus hermanos le dio ropa nueva. Pero a Benjamín le dio cinco mudas de ropa nueva y {{units:unos 3,5 kilos|300 siclos}} de plata.

fr.L: À eux tous, à chacun, il donna des vêtements de rechange ; mais à Benjamin il donna 300 [sicles] d’argent et cinq vêtements de rechange.
fr.B: Il donna à chacun d’eux un habit neuf, mais à Benjamin il donna {{units:environ 3,5 kilos|300 sicles}} d’argent et cinq habits neufs.
fr.R: Il a donné des vêtements neufs à chacun de ses frères. Mais à Benjamin, il a donné cinq habits neufs et {{units:environ 3,5 kilos|300 sicles}} d’argent.

sw.L: Wote aliwapa, kila mtu, mavazi ya kubadilisha; lakini Benyamini alimpa [shekeli] 300 za fedha na mavazi matano ya kubadilisha.
sw.B: Alimpa kila mmoja wao vazi jipya, lakini Benyamini alimpa {{units:karibu kilo 3.5|shekeli 300}} za fedha na mavazi matano.
sw.R: Kila mmoja wa ndugu zake alimpa nguo mpya. Lakini Benyamini alimpa mavazi mapya matano na {{units:karibu kilo 3.5|shekeli 300}} za fedha.

decisions.choice: changes of clothes: fine garments for festive wear
decisions.reason: A "change" of clothing was a fine set to put on in place of everyday wear, a costly gift.

decisions.choice: more for Benjamin: favoritism without envy
decisions.reason: Joseph, once hated for his father's favor and his special robe (37:3-4), now openly favors Benjamin. The brothers' acceptance shows how far they have come.

decisions.choice: about 7.5 pounds of silver; with the Measures setting, 300 shekels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "three hundred of silver"; shekels, about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams) each, are meant. Balanced and Readable give the modern weight by default; Literal keeps the original.

source.text: וּלְאָבִ֞יו שָׁלַ֤ח כְּזֹאת֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה חֲמֹרִ֔ים נֹשְׂאִ֖ים מִטּ֣וּב מִצְרָ֑יִם וְעֶ֣שֶׂר אֲתֹנֹ֡ת נֹֽ֠שְׂאֹת בָּ֣ר וָלֶ֧חֶם וּמָז֛וֹן לְאָבִ֖יו לַדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to his father he sent according to this: ten donkeys carrying of [the] good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain and bread and provision for his father for the way.

en.L: And to his father he sent as follows: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread and provisions for his father for the journey.
en.B: To his father he sent the same, and more: ten donkeys laden with the finest goods of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread and food for his father's journey.
en.R: He also sent his father ten donkeys carrying the best things from Egypt. And he sent ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread and other food for his father's trip.

es.L: Y a su padre le envió de esta manera: diez asnos cargados de las cosas buenas de Egipto, y diez asnas cargadas de grano, pan y provisiones para su padre para el camino.
es.B: A su padre le envió lo mismo, y más: diez burros cargados con los mejores productos de Egipto, y diez burras cargadas de grano, pan y alimentos para el viaje de su padre.
es.R: También le envió a su padre diez burros cargados con las mejores cosas de Egipto. Y le mandó diez burras cargadas de grano, pan y otros alimentos para el viaje.

fr.L: Et à son père il envoya ceci : dix ânes chargés des bonnes choses de l’Égypte, et dix ânesses chargées de grain, de pain et de vivres pour son père, pour la route.
fr.B: À son père il envoya de même, et davantage : dix ânes chargés des meilleurs produits de l’Égypte, et dix ânesses portant du grain, du pain et des provisions pour le voyage de son père.
fr.R: Il a aussi envoyé à son père dix ânes chargés des meilleures choses de l’Égypte. Et il a envoyé dix ânesses chargées de grain, de pain et d’autres provisions pour le voyage de son père.

sw.L: Na kwa baba yake alipeleka hivi: punda kumi waliobeba vitu vizuri vya Misri, na punda jike kumi waliobeba nafaka na mkate na chakula kwa ajili ya baba yake kwa safari.
sw.B: Kwa baba yake alipeleka vivyo hivyo, na zaidi: punda kumi waliotwikwa vitu bora vya Misri, na punda jike kumi waliobeba nafaka, mikate na chakula cha safari ya baba yake.
sw.R: Pia alimpelekea baba yake punda kumi waliobeba vitu bora kutoka Misri. Akapeleka na punda jike kumi waliobeba nafaka, mikate na vyakula vingine kwa ajili ya safari ya baba yake.

decisions.choice: according to this: likewise, or as follows
decisions.reason: Kezot can mean "likewise" (gifts like those just given) or "as follows" (introducing the list). Either way the list follows.

source.text: וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־אֶחָ֖יו וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַֽל־תִּרְגְּז֖וּ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent off his brothers and they went, and he said to them, do not be agitated on the way.

en.L: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed, and he said to them, "Do not quarrel on the way."
en.B: Then he sent his brothers off, and as they left he told them, "Do not argue with each other on the way."
en.R: Then Joseph sent his brothers on their way. As they left he said, "Do not fight with each other on the trip!"

es.L: Y despidió a sus hermanos, y se fueron, y les dijo: «No {{plural_you:riñan|riñáis}} en el camino».
es.B: Luego despidió a sus hermanos, y mientras se iban les dijo: «No {{plural_you:discutan|discutáis}} entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por el camino».
es.R: Después José despidió a sus hermanos. Cuando se iban, les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:No se peleen|No os peleéis}} durante el viaje!».

fr.L: Et il renvoya ses frères, et ils partirent, et il leur dit : « Ne vous querellez pas en chemin. »
fr.B: Puis il laissa partir ses frères, et, au moment où ils s’en allaient, il leur dit : « Ne vous disputez pas en route. »
fr.R: Puis Joseph a laissé partir ses frères. Au moment où ils s’en allaient, il leur a dit : « Pas de disputes entre vous pendant le voyage ! »

sw.L: Akawaaga ndugu zake, nao wakaenda; akawaambia, "Msigombane njiani."
sw.B: Kisha akawaaga ndugu zake, na walipokuwa wakiondoka akawaambia, "Msibishane njiani."
sw.R: Kisha Yusufu akawaaga ndugu zake. Walipokuwa wakiondoka akawaambia, "Msigombane mkiwa safarini!"

decisions.choice: do not quarrel: or, do not be afraid
decisions.reason: Ragaz means to be stirred up or agitated, whether by anger or by fear. Joseph may be warning them not to blame one another over the past, or reassuring them that they have nothing to fear on the road. The first fits the brothers' history (42:22).

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲבִיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went up from Egypt and came [to the] land of Canaan to Jacob their father.

en.L: And they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob.
en.B: So they left Egypt and went up to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.
en.R: They left Egypt and went back to their father Jacob in Canaan.

es.L: Y subieron de Egipto, y llegaron a la tierra de Canaán, a Jacob su padre.
es.B: Así que salieron de Egipto y subieron hasta donde estaba su padre Jacob, en la tierra de Canaán.
es.R: Salieron de Egipto y volvieron a Canaán, donde estaba su padre Jacob.

fr.L: Et ils montèrent d’Égypte et arrivèrent au pays de Canaan, auprès de Jacob leur père.
fr.B: Ils quittèrent donc l’Égypte et remontèrent vers leur père Jacob, au pays de Canaan.
fr.R: Ils sont partis d’Égypte et ils sont retournés en Canaan, chez leur père Jacob.

sw.L: Wakapanda kutoka Misri, wakafika nchi ya Kanaani kwa Yakobo baba yao.
sw.B: Basi wakaondoka Misri, wakapanda mpaka kwa baba yao Yakobo katika nchi ya Kanaani.
sw.R: Wakaondoka Misri, wakarudi Kanaani kwa baba yao Yakobo.

source.text: וַיַּגִּ֨דוּ ל֜וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר ע֚וֹד יוֹסֵ֣ף חַ֔י וְכִֽי־ה֥וּא מֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֣פָג לִבּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י לֹא־הֶאֱמִ֖ין לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they told him, saying, still Joseph [is] alive, and that he [is] ruling over all [the] land of Egypt. And grew numb his heart, for not did he believe them.

en.L: And they told him, "Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt." And his heart went numb, for he did not believe them.
en.B: "Joseph is alive!" they told him. "He is governor of the whole land of Egypt!" Jacob was stunned; he could not believe them.
en.R: They told him, "Joseph is still alive! He is the ruler of all Egypt!" Jacob was so shocked that he felt nothing. He did not believe them.

es.L: Y le contaron: «José aún vive, y él gobierna sobre toda la tierra de Egipto». Y su corazón se quedó helado, porque no les creía.
es.B: «¡José está vivo!», le dijeron. «¡Es el gobernador de todo Egipto!». Jacob se quedó atónito; no podía creerles.
es.R: Le dijeron: «¡José todavía vive! ¡Es el gobernador de todo Egipto!». Jacob se impresionó tanto que se quedó como paralizado. No les creía.

fr.L: Et ils lui racontèrent : « Joseph est encore vivant, et c’est lui qui gouverne tout le pays d’Égypte. » Et son cœur resta glacé, car il ne les croyait pas.
fr.B: « Joseph est vivant ! lui dirent-ils. Il gouverne toute l’Égypte ! » Jacob resta interdit ; il ne pouvait pas les croire.
fr.R: Ils lui ont dit : « Joseph est toujours vivant ! C’est lui qui commande toute l’Égypte ! » Jacob a eu un tel choc qu’il ne sentait plus rien. Il ne les croyait pas.

sw.L: Wakamwambia, "Yusufu bado yu hai, naye ndiye anayetawala nchi yote ya Misri." Moyo wake ukaganda, kwa maana hakuwasadiki.
sw.B: "Yusufu yu hai!" wakamwambia. "Yeye ndiye mtawala wa nchi yote ya Misri!" Yakobo akapigwa na bumbuazi; hakuweza kuwaamini.
sw.R: Wakamwambia, "Yusufu bado anaishi! Yeye ni mtawala wa Misri yote!" Yakobo alishtuka mno hata akawa kama hasikii chochote. Hakuwaamini.

decisions.choice: his heart grew numb: he was stunned
decisions.reason: Puq means to grow cold or numb. The news is too great for Jacob to take in.

source.text: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו אֵ֣ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֤י יוֹסֵף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֲגָל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח יוֹסֵ֖ף לָשֵׂ֣את אֹת֑וֹ וַתְּחִ֕י ר֖וּחַ יַעֲקֹ֥ב אֲבִיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they spoke to him all [the] words of Joseph which he had spoken to them; and he saw the carts which Joseph had sent to carry him, and revived [the] spirit of Jacob their father.

en.L: But when they told him all the words that Joseph had spoken to them, and when he saw the carts that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.
en.B: But when they repeated to him everything Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the carts Joseph had sent to carry him, their father Jacob's spirit came back to life.
en.R: But then they told him everything Joseph had said to them. And Jacob saw the wagons Joseph had sent to bring him to Egypt. Then their father Jacob felt alive again.

es.L: Pero cuando le dijeron todas las palabras que José les había dicho, y cuando vio los carros que José había enviado para llevarlo, revivió el espíritu de su padre Jacob.
es.B: Pero cuando le repitieron todo lo que José les había dicho, y cuando vio los carros que José había enviado para llevarlo, el espíritu de su padre Jacob volvió a la vida.
es.R: Pero luego le contaron todo lo que José les había dicho. Y Jacob vio las carretas que José había mandado para llevarlo a Egipto. Entonces su padre Jacob volvió a sentirse vivo.

fr.L: Mais quand ils lui eurent dit toutes les paroles que Joseph leur avait dites, et qu’il vit les chariots que Joseph avait envoyés pour le transporter, l’esprit de Jacob leur père se ranima.
fr.B: Mais lorsqu’ils lui eurent répété tout ce que Joseph leur avait dit, et qu’il vit les chariots que Joseph avait envoyés pour l’emmener, l’esprit de leur père Jacob reprit vie.
fr.R: Mais ensuite, ils lui ont raconté tout ce que Joseph leur avait dit. Et Jacob a vu les chariots que Joseph avait envoyés pour l’emmener en Égypte. Alors leur père Jacob s’est senti revivre.

sw.L: Lakini walipomwambia maneno yote ya Yusufu aliyowaambia, naye alipoyaona magari ambayo Yusufu aliyatuma kumchukua, roho ya Yakobo baba yao ikahuika.
sw.B: Lakini walipomweleza kila kitu Yusufu alichowaambia, na alipoyaona magari Yusufu aliyoyatuma ili kumchukua, roho ya baba yao Yakobo ikarudiwa na uhai.
sw.R: Lakini kisha wakamweleza yote Yusufu aliyowaambia. Naye Yakobo akaona magari Yusufu aliyoyatuma ili kumpeleka Misri. Hapo baba yao Yakobo akajisikia kuwa hai tena.

decisions.choice: his spirit revived: life and hope returned
decisions.reason: Ruach, "spirit" or "breath", is a person's vital energy. Jacob, who had expected to go down to Sheol mourning (37:35), comes back to life.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רַ֛ב עוֹד־יוֹסֵ֥ף בְּנִ֖י חָ֑י אֵֽלְכָ֥ה וְאֶרְאֶ֖נּוּ בְּטֶ֥רֶם אָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Israel, enough! Still Joseph my son [is] alive. I will go and see him before I die.

en.L: And Israel said, "It is enough; Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."
en.B: "Enough!" said Israel. "My son Joseph is still alive! I will go and see him before I die."
en.R: Then Israel said, "Now I believe it! My son Joseph is still alive! I will go and see him before I die."

es.L: Y dijo Israel: «¡Basta! José mi hijo vive todavía. Iré y lo veré antes de morir».
es.B: «¡Me basta!», exclamó Israel. «¡Mi hijo José todavía vive! Iré a verlo antes de morir».
es.R: Entonces Israel dijo: «¡Ahora sí lo creo! ¡Mi hijo José todavía está vivo! Iré a verlo antes de morirme».

fr.L: Et Israël dit : « C’est assez ! Joseph mon fils est encore vivant. J’irai et je le verrai avant de mourir. »
fr.B: « Il ne m’en faut pas plus ! dit Israël. Mon fils Joseph est encore en vie ! J’irai le voir avant de mourir. »
fr.R: Alors Israël a dit : « Maintenant, je le crois ! Mon fils Joseph est toujours vivant ! Je vais aller le voir avant de mourir. »

sw.L: Israeli akasema, "Yatosha! Yusufu mwanangu bado yu hai. Nitakwenda nimwone kabla sijafa."
sw.B: Israeli akasema, "Inatosha! Mwanangu Yusufu bado yu hai! Nitakwenda nikamwone kabla sijafa."
sw.R: Kisha Israeli akasema, "Sasa naamini! Mwanangu Yusufu bado anaishi! Nitakwenda kumwona kabla sijafa."

decisions.choice: Israel: Jacob's covenant name
decisions.reason: The narrator switches from "Jacob" (verse 27) to "Israel" as the father revives and decides to go. The name God gave him (32:28; 35:10) marks him as the father of the people.

decisions.choice: enough: I am convinced, I need nothing more
decisions.reason: Rav here expresses that Jacob needs no further proof; or perhaps that this one fact is all he asks.
